column1: # The rules of the channel rename map format, and which reader enforces each.
# Two readers, one format: QmxFindingGate\Tsv + RenameMaps (scripts/finding-gate/, not on the
# production autoloader) and Qualimetrix\Analysis\Policy\Baseline\ChannelRenameMap (shipped with
# baseline:rename-channels, reads a map a user was given with their upgrade). "They read the same
# format" is therefore a claim about two code paths.
# What makes it checkable is one corpus of lines run against both:
# tests/Analysis/Policy/Baseline/Fixtures/ChannelRenameTsvCorpus.php, asserted by
# ChannelRenameMapTest (product side) and ChannelRenameTsvGateAgreementTest (gate side). Every row
# below names its corpus case. A change to either reader that moves a verdict has to move a row
# here; a rule added to one reader without a row here is the failure this file exists to expose.
# Five rows are deliberate divergences, marked DIVERGENCE with the reason. None is an oversight:
# the gate translates artifacts and the carry writes a file, and the asymmetry follows from that.
rule
header is exactly old/new/reason
column5: The header names the columns; a different one is a different file.

column1: a row has exactly three tab-separated fields
column5: A row without a reason is a rename nobody justified.

column1: no whitespace around any field
column5: Matching is exact equality, so an invisible edge fires nowhere and would be reported as an idle declaration.

column1: a trailing CR is stripped per line
column5: A CRLF checkout is not a defect.

column1: blank lines and # comments are skipped
a header with no rows is a valid map
column5: A map that declares nothing is a map.

column1: both sides of a row equal
column5: A declaration that states no rename.

column1: two rows rename one old name
column5: What the old name carries to becomes undecidable.

column1: one row's target is renamed again by another
column5: The result would depend on the order rows were applied in.

column1: two old names onto one new name
column5: DIVERGENCE. channels.tsv is forward-only (RenameMaps::FILES), and forwards a collapse is a true statement: two reference names really do become one. A carry writes a file, and a file cannot hold two accepted ceilings for one identity.

column1: the same (old, new) row twice
column5: DIVERGENCE. RenameMaps::normalize() groups rows by (old, new) so one name may be declared in two maps and still count once. A carry reads one map, where a repeated old name is the ambiguity the rule above forbids.

column1: the retired rule#code spelling
column5: DIVERGENCE. The gate still expands the retired pair spelling because a reference tree predating the change publishes it. A baseline never did: its channel field holds a code, and FindingChannel refuses the pair spelling.

column1: an empty new field
column5: DIVERGENCE. The gate checks a field for whitespace edges, not for being a name; the carry constructs a FindingChannel, and an empty channel does not exist.

column1: a name carrying the level separator ':'
column5: DIVERGENCE. ':' addresses a level beside a channel name and can never be part of one, which only the product type knows.

column1: a name carrying the ASCII Unit Separator
column5: BaselineIdentity reserves it as its key separator. No corpus case runs it against the gate: a TSV field cannot usefully carry it and the gate has no opinion either way.
